name: marine_propeller_autonomous
description: Fully autonomous aggressive propeller — the prompt describes geometry + service context only. The agent derives ALL boundary conditions itself (shaft-seat fixture, thrust + torque on the blades) and declares them in spec.load_cases, plus declares the shaft mount (bore + keyway) in spec.features. fem declares NOTHING (use_parent_fallbacks): fem_loadcases verifies the resolved physics of the agent's own load model.

stages.prompt:
5-blade AGGRESSIVE high-pitch skewed marine propeller (aluminium bronze / 6061), parametric — built for maximum volume flow, right-handed rotation about +Z.

Frame: hub axis along Z, bottom face on the XY plane (z = 0), centred in X and Y. mm.
- Ø140 propeller: blade tips touch the r = 70 cylinder; overall bounding box ~137-140 in X and Y (a 5-fold rotor cannot put tips on both + and - of one axis) and exactly 28 in Z: z = 0..28.
- Central cylindrical hub: outer dia 30 (r = 15), height 28 (z = 0..28).
- SHAFT MOUNT — a real bore + keyway seat, not a plain hole: concentric through-bore dia 10 (r = 5) along Z through (0,0), open on both z = 0 and z = 28 (bore cylinder height ~36 centred at z = 14 so it clears both faces), PLUS one axial keyway slot along the full bore height: 3.0 mm wide, ~1.8 mm deep radially into the bore wall (DIN 6885-1 keyway for a Ø10 shaft — a rectangular slot cut into the wall parallel to Z, spanning z = 0..28).
- 5 identical skewed, strongly twisted hydrofoil blades spaced 0/72/144/216/288 deg around Z:
  * Each blade runs radially from r = 9 (root station 6 mm inside the r = 15 hub wall — a fat union overlap; still 4 mm clear of the r = 5 bore) out to tip radius r = 70 (bound the tip to the r = 70 cylinder).
  * Loft each blade across >= 4 radial stations (e.g. r = 9, 30, 55, 70) using thin hydrofoil/elliptical sections: chord ~30 at the root tapering to ~24 at the tip (BIG blade area — wide aggressive foil), thickness at every station >= 3.0 mm (target 3.0-3.4 mm).
  * HIGH PITCH for maximum flow: progressive helicoidal twist ~58 deg at the root station decreasing to ~38 deg at the tip (pitch = angle between the section chord line and the XY plane). Rotate each section about its own RADIAL stacking axis — the line from the hub axis through the section's mid-chord point — so pitch only changes a point's (tangential, z) position and NEVER its radius.
  * SKEW: each section's mid-chord point additionally lags backwards tangentially, 0 deg at the root growing to ~22 deg at the tip (strongly swept tips like an aggressive skewed runner). Apply skew as a PURE ROTATION about the Z axis through (0,0): rotate every point of the section by the skew angle — never translate tangentially — so each station keeps its exact radius and the tip stays pinned to the r = 70 cylinder. Pitch+skew leave radii invariant — if tips over- or undershoot the Ø140 envelope, the section's radial extent (not the rotations) is wrong.
  * Keep ALL blade geometry strictly inside z = 2..26 so the flat hub faces define the exact z = 0..28 height.
  * Prefer the reviewed helper over hand-rolled section transforms: cadlib.radial_blade(n_blades=5, root_r=9.0, tip_r=70.0, chord=(30.0, 24.0), thickness=(3.4, 3.0), pitch_root_deg=58.0, pitch_tip_deg=38.0, skew_tip_deg=22.0, z=14.0) encodes exactly this radial-axis pitch + pure-azimuth skew by construction (its `stations` list can also express a non-linear schedule); only fall back to manual lofts if the helper cannot express the section you need.
- Union the 5 blades with the hub, then cut the dia-10 bore AND the keyway. Blades are SOLID bodies — do not cut slots, channels, weight pockets or voids into them. No fillets, no chamfers; the result must be a single watertight, VALID solid centred on the origin. Before finishing verify result.bounding_box() spans ~-70..+70 on both X and Y and is symmetric about (0,0) — adjust the tip station's radial extent, not the hub; if the fused body has invalid faces rebuild the loft with smoother/fewer sections or deeper root overlap.

SERVICE CONTEXT — derive the structural model yourself: this propeller bolts onto a boat shaft through the keyed Ø10 bore and spins right-handed about +Z. Typical service: axial thrust of several hundred N distributed over the blade surfaces (the water pushes the blades along +Z), plus drive torque of ~25 N·m about Z transmitted through the shaft/keyway. YOU decide the load cases, the fixed supports (shaft seat = the bore+keyway wall), the load regions/mechanisms and the magnitudes — declare them all in spec.load_cases. Also declare the machined interfaces (through-bore, keyway) in spec.features with position, axis, diameter and depth so post-processing can re-cut them exactly.
